intervals.quote: KIMS and DM-Ice have joined to construct and operate a single experiment, named COSINE, at the Yangyang underground laboratory (Y2L) in Korea.

placements.quote: The assembled detector modules are installed in the shielding structure that was used for the KIMS CsI(Tl) detector measurements at the Yangyang Underground Laboratory (Y2L)

exposure.quote: obtained with a 2967.4 kg*day data exposure

target_medium.quote: NaI(Tl) detectors at the Yangyang Underground Laboratory

summary.plain: KIMS-NaI was the sodium-iodide stage of the Korean KIMS programme: the team grew its own low-radioactivity crystals, tested them underground at Yangyang and set dark-matter limits with two of them. A planned 200 kg array became, together with a US group, the COSINE-100 experiment.
summary.technical: NaI(Tl) crystal development and WIMP search at Y2L in the shield previously used for KIMS-CsI: two crystals (8.26 kg and 9.15 kg), 2967.4 kg d (November 2013 - January 2015), pulse-shape discrimination of nuclear recoils; limits partially exclude the DAMA/LIBRA allowed region for WIMP-sodium scattering. A 200 kg array was planned (arXiv:1510.04519).

technology.quote: The crystals are encapsulated in a cylindrical copper structure with quartz windows at each end.
technology.value: Low-background NaI(Tl) scintillating crystals read by two photomultiplier tubes, with pulse-shape discrimination
